reading.title: Many Ways to Look
reading.purpose: Explore how exact verbs show the difference between a quick look, a stare, and careful study.
paras: The word "look" is handy, yet it does not tell how someone uses their eyes. English has sharper verbs that show speed, feeling, and focus all at once.

Some verbs show a very brief look. You glance at a wall clock for just a second to check the time. You might peek through a crack in a door to catch a quick view of a surprise cake. When you want one name on a long list, you scan the page quickly from top to bottom.

Other verbs show how your eyes handle bright light or fog. Stepping into strong noon sun makes you squint, narrowing your eyes partly shut. In dim light, you lean forward and peer closely at tiny print on a map because it is hard to see.

Looking can also show mood or careful work. If someone cuts in line, a person might glare with an angry stare. On a clear night, stargazers gaze steadily at the constellations for a long time. Scientists observe ants to learn how they carry crumbs. Hikers send a leader ahead to scout the trail and check for fallen logs. Anyone who sees a meteor streak across the sky with their own eyes is lucky to witness it.
Choosing the right looking verb turns a plain sentence into a clear picture.

choices: to look at someone with a very angry stare
to narrow your eyes partly shut
to search a long page quickly for one name
to walk ahead on a trail to check for logs
qs.why: Paragraph 3 explains that strong noon sun makes you squint, "narrowing your eyes partly shut."

qs.q: Priya runs her eyes rapidly down a bus schedule to find Route 14. Which verb from the reading best fits what Priya is doing?

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Stargazers and scientists use their eyes much more carefully than hikers do.
Exact looking verbs show speed, mood, and focus better than the word look.
Bright noon sun and dim indoor maps are the hardest things for eyes to handle.
Writers should never use the word look anywhere inside a school essay.
